Name: FarmLink - LAN Server Discovery
Author: sjohnson1021
Description:
[size=6][b]FarmLink[/b][/size]

Swapping IP addresses to play co-op is a chore. [b]FarmLink[/b] removes that step. Host a game and you appear in your friends' Co-op menu automatically, along with the farm name, who is hosting, and how full the farm is. Click the entry to join.

Install it on both computers and you are done. There is nothing to configure.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/41128/41128-1768081089-1326374354.png[/img]
[size=5][b]In the Co-op menu, where you would expect it[/b][/size]
Farms found on your network are listed under [b]Co-op -> Join[/b] alongside everything else.

[list]
[*][b]Nothing to set up.[/b] The settings menu exists for unusual networks, not for normal ones.[/*]
[*][b]The details you want:[/b] farm name, host, player count, and address.[/*]
[*][b]The right farm icon[/b] for Standard, Beach, Riverland and the rest, including farm types added by other mods.[/*]
[*][b]No firewall rule.[/b] Older versions asked you to open a port by hand. That step is gone.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Friends who are somewhere else[/b][/size]

FarmLink also works over a virtual network, so local co-op doesn't have to mean the same building.

[list]
[*][b]Tailscale[/b] needs no configuration. Machines on your tailnet are found the same way machines on your home network are. This was tested on two computers on genuinely separate connections, one on home broadband and one on a phone hotspot.[/*]
[*][b]ZeroTier[/b] works, and is slower. Give it ten or fifteen seconds in the Co-op menu rather than one or two.[/*]
[*][b]Hamachi and Radmin VPN[/b] are expected to work but have not been verified. They create a virtual network adapter in much the same way ZeroTier does, and that is the part FarmLink depends on.[/*]
[*][b]Anything else:[/b] put your friend's address into [b]Extra Addresses[/b] and FarmLink will check it directly. This route doesn't rely on the VPN carrying broadcast traffic, so it still works where automatic discovery doesn't.[/*]
[/list]
When a friend is reachable both on your home network and over a VPN, FarmLink now uses the
home network rather than whichever answered first.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/41128/41128-1785895810-999293024.png[/img]
[size=5][b]Settings[/b][/size]
There are three, through [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b], and most people never open them.

[list]
[*][b]Enable LAN Server Discovery[/b] turns the whole thing off if you would rather type addresses yourself.[/*]
[*][b]Extra Addresses[/b] is usually empty. Put an address here for a VPN that FarmLink cannot find on its own.[/*]
[*][b]Network Adapters[/b] starts with everything ticked, which is right for almost everyone.[/*]
[/list]
That last one is a privacy setting. When you host, FarmLink announces your farm name and your character's name over each ticked adapter so that friends can find you. If the machine has a work VPN on it, a corporate Wi-Fi profile, or a connection you pay for by
the megabyte, untick it and FarmLink will stay off it completely.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/41128/41128-1785895810-1434211454.png[/img]
Unticking an adapter never helps anyone find you. All it does is stop you being announced somewhere. Adapters you add later are used automatically, so a VPN you install next month needs no attention.

[size=5][b]What changed in 2.0[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Works across Tailscale and ZeroTier instead of one home network.[/*]
[*]Joining no longer needs a firewall rule, because FarmLink sets the connection up itself.[/*]
[*]Discovery was rebuilt on DNS-SD, the standard used for this everywhere else. Farms turn up faster and get through firewalls that used to block them.[/*]
[*]The adapter picker is back as a privacy setting rather than a troubleshooting one, and as a list you tick rather than a single choice.[/*]
[*][b]Removed:[/b] Broadcast Interval, Broadcast Port, Game Port, and Broadcast Across All Adapters. The first two stopped meaning anything when discovery moved to the standard port. Game Port never worked, because Stardew hardcodes it, so changing it only broke your own join address. Old settings still sitting in [font=Courier New]config.json[/font] are ignored and nothing needs migrating.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]What isn't proven yet[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Hamachi and Radmin VPN.[/b] Very likely fine, for the reason above, but nobody has run them. If one of them doesn't work, [b]Extra Addresses[/b] will still get you connected.[/*]
[*][b]Some Wi-Fi networks block this kind of traffic.[/b] Guest networks and a few mesh systems drop it. [b]Extra Addresses[/b] is the way around that too. [b]Linux has had the most testing.[/b] Windows and macOS use the same standard mechanism and should behave, but they have had less use.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Requires [b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b] and [b]SMAPI 4.0+[/b].[/*]
[*]Works with [b]all modded farm types[/b]. Custom icons load if the farm's author provided one.[/*]
[*]Works with [b]Split Screen[/b]. Discovery switches itself off there to keep the menu tidy.[/*]
[*][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] is optional, and only needed if you want to change settings in game.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Source code[/b][/size]
[url=https://github.com/sjohnson1021/FarmLink]FarmLink on GitHub[/url], including what was measured, what wasn't, and why several tempting ideas were rejected.

Downloads.Description: Zip containing the mod files, extract to your Mods folder, and enjoy.

Manifest.Name: FarmLink
Manifest.Description: Broadcasts your co-op farm to the local network when hosting, and discovers co-op farms on the local network.
Manifest.Author: Sean Johnson

Downloads.Description: Revised 2.0 version, which works over TailScale, ZeroTier, and other network overlays/VPN-like software. Should not require manual firewall/port configuration.

Manifest.Name: FarmLink
Manifest.Description: Announces your co-op farm on the local network when hosting, and lists the farms it finds in the co-op menu, using standard DNS-SD service discovery.
Manifest.Author: Sean Johnson
